text: Chapter 1: Conductive Reasoning The second ring of the facility was unusually quiet — just the low, rhythmic hum of overhead fluorescents and the faint echo of someone vaulting something three rooms over. Herman didn’t care. He had more pressing problems. Namely, the flailing cop draped over one shoulder, and the freshly sabotaged hook directly in his path. The hook had clattered to the ground just as the Doctor rounded the corner, Leon kicking and struggling wildly on his shoulder. He had finally started to come around fully from the baton strike that set him prone and was now well on his way to breaking Herman's grip on his waistline. Jake had just finished dismantling it — fast fingers, smug grin — and the nuisance flipped Herman off before vanishing down a side hallway, feet barely touching the tile, content to make the Doctor's job as difficult as physically possible. “Great,” Herman muttered, voice thick with irritation and exhaustion. “Just great.” Herman exhaled slowly through his teeth and adjusted his grip as Leon squirmed again, staggering slightly to the side as a knee almost hit his head, and surveyed the area. The next closest hook was too far off, and the basement with its indestructible hook quartet was clearly out of range. But this particular survivor was one of those. Not fast. Not loud. Not even slippery. Just — gone, the second he got loose. A ghost in denim and bruises. He did not have the patience to track him down yet again before the gates could release him back to the Fog. The Entity was annoyed enough with how often survivors escaped lately. It wouldn't serve him to let this one loose in the halls. Herman ripped Leon, still flailing, from his shoulder and threw him at a locker. He hit the edge of the wood with a sharp crack, the impact knocking the wind from him and kicking the door open to catch him a second time on the way down. Dazed, Leon rolled onto his back, trying to refocus his eyes before finding himself being hoisted up again. "Nothing personal, Mr. Kennedy. I would have preferred to use a basement hook and be done with this chase. But you seem particularly animated today and I am not in the mood to roll an ankle on the steps with your wriggling about." He navigated into a nearby room, dumping Leon heavily against the cabinets on one wall. Old carts littered the space — rusted gurneys with half-locked wheels, trays with upturned pans, a few overturned IV poles resting like skeletal limbs along the walls. The air stank faintly of dust and ozone, like a place struck by lightning long ago and left to rot. It would serve perfectly to keep this particular migraine contained for the time being, he mused to himself as he crouched to rummage through the pouches at the man’s waist. The pest always had some kind of random item on hand that the Entity hadn't deemed important enough to remove; and sure enough, in one of the stained and battered hip pouches, he found a set of bright silver handcuffs. These soldier types were always so predictable. Real steel, not prop bullshit. The Entity must’ve let them pass without flagging their intent. Or maybe she just liked what they could do when repurposed. "You have a nasty habit of vanishing into the dust when I stop looking, and I have a quota to fill today. Therefore, you are going to wait right here until I can locate your little saboteur friend and ensure that he can no longer disable the tools I require to do my job." A painful wrenching tug on his shoulder to pull him to his feet, and a sharp click, and Leon was secured to a padlocked cabinet by one wrist. He winced against the strain on his shoulder, pulling himself into a heavy lean against the cabinet and trying to shake off the gray at the edges of his vision from the earlier impact. Herman frowned slightly at the glassy expression in Leon's eyes and briefly touched his baton to the cabinet. CRACK . The charge arced through the cabinet and into the cuff in an instant. Leon jolted — back arching, breath catching in his throat like it had been yanked by force. A small sound escaped him — half growl, half gasp — and then he sagged again, panting. Wide-eyed. Awake. Much better. "Rise and shine, Mr. Kennedy. The Entity prefers her meals still screaming, afterall. It won't do for you to be too concussed to appreciate her attention, now, would it? Now if you'll excuse me, I have a pest to find. Once I locate him, I'll be sure to bring him here so I can fry him personally at your feet for the grievous insult of interfering with my work. Then we can resume from where we left off. Don't go anywhere, now!" And with that, the Doctor stormed out of the room to continue his hunt, his manic giggle floating down the hallway with the diminishing terror radius, leaving Leon dazed and tugging at his own cuffs as they dug angry red marks into his wrist. He let out a hiss as the motion pulled too fast, too far, the shoulder lighting up in protest. Not dislocated, but close enough to threaten it if he got clever. The wrist burned. It wasn’t the surface sting — he’d felt that before. From tasers, from volts, from the Doctor’s regular blasts — it was deeper . An ache curling through tendon and bone, buzzing in the socket of his shoulder. Leon blinked hard, the afterimage of that electric snap still painting sharp edges behind his eyelids. The world tilted, but settled. "Ok, less than ideal..." Leon twisted at the cuff experimentally. Nothing. No give in the chain, no flex in the cabinet.
